observation.description: The core chat sidebar query — 'the private channels I belong to' — is inexpressible against the membership declaration: membershipResource.rowField() refuses both a nonexistent field and the resource table's own '_id' (QUERY_MEMBERSHIP_RESOURCE_REF_INVALID: 'membership row field _id does not exist on channels'), and the arg() form gates one known channel rather than listing. There is also no non-throwing role test in JS handlers (requireRole denial is terminal), so a handler cannot filter rows by membership either. The arm was forced to maintain a parallel app-data channelSeats mirror in every membership-touching mutation — adjacent to the roster mirror the scoped-roles guide explicitly warns against — purely for listing.

competitorOutcome.description: The frozen Convex chat arm modeled memberships as ordinary readable documents, so 'channels I belong to' was one indexed reactive query with no mirror; its cost was that membership privacy/authority is app-convention rather than host-owned.

mustNotRegress: The private-roster posture itself: no existence oracle, no enumerable roster, denial that does not disclose whether the resource exists.
smallestCoherentFix: A declaration-owned self-scoped projection — e.g. a generated 'myMemberships(declaration)' live query (or membershipResource.self() joinable against the resource table) that returns only the caller's own seats with their resource ids and roles, revocation-active like requireRole. That is the caller's own rows, so it does not breach the privacy posture.
acceptanceWitness: An external app declares a resource-scoped membership and renders 'my channels' from one generated query, with an acceptance check that another principal's seats never appear and that self-removal live-updates the list — no app-data mirror table present.
